results.title: PCB Tariffs from China to the US in 2026: HTS Codes ...
results.content:
PCB tariffs from China can significantly change the real cost of a U.S.-bound order before your boards reach production. A quote may look competitive at the factory level, but the final landed cost depends on the Harmonized Tariff Schedule (HTS) code, Section 301 duty, freight, customs fees, and exclusion status. For bare printed circuit boards (PCBs), classification typically starts with HTS 8534. For some PCB assemblies (PCBAs), HTS 8473.30 may apply, though classification depends on the [...] Bare PCBs usually fall under HTS 8534.00, but layer count, material, and board type still affect the correct subheading.
 Some PCBAs may fall under HTS 8473.30 when they are printed circuit assemblies for automatic data processing equipment, but many PCBAs use other classifications.
 China-origin PCBs and some PCBAs can face a 25% Section 301 tariff unless a valid exclusion applies. [...] A printed circuit board assembly includes mounted components such as integrated circuits, resistors, capacitors, connectors, sensors, processors, or memory devices. Some PCBAs fall under HTS 8473.30 when they are printed circuit assemblies suitable for use with automatic data processing machines. However, not every PCBA belongs there.

results.title: HS Code for Printed Circuit Boards (PCB)
results.content: Bare printed circuit boards under heading 8534 enter the United States duty-free at a 0% general rate, across all the layer, substrate and flexible-type breakouts. Because the regular duty is free, the reason to identify the precise 10-digit code is accurate statistical reporting. Note that populated boards (printed circuit assemblies) are classified elsewhere as parts of the host device and may carry different duty treatment, and separate trade measures can apply to circuit boards and [...] Bare (unpopulated) printed circuit boards are classified under HTS heading 8534, the dedicated provision for printed circuits. All bare PCBs are duty-free, with the 10-digit statistical breakouts distinguishing the board by the number of conductive layers, the substrate (impregnated paper, ceramic or other), and whether the board is the flexible type. An important distinction is that heading 8534 is for the bare board only; once components are mounted to create a printed circuit assembly, the [...] assembly, the populated board is generally classified as a part of the device it belongs to, not under 8534.

Printed Circuit Board Assemblies:

Assembled PCBs containing components are classified under HS code 85177090 in most cases. This includes assembled rigid boards and rigid-flex assemblies. If incorporating high-value components like processors, use 85176290.

 Heading 8534 covers bare or unfinished printed circuit boards.

 The first 2 digits indicate the broad PCB category.
 The next 2 digits specify attributes like layer count, board type, and assembly status.
 The final 2-4 digits provide additional technical distinctions. results.title: A Complete Guide to PCB Board HS Code Classification
results.content:
### What Is the Biggest Mistake Shippers Make?

Hands down, the most common and costly error is classifying a populated Printed Circuit Board Assembly (PCBA) as a bare board under HS 8534. This one slip-up is responsible for a huge number of customs holds and fines. [...] | Region/Country | Example Tariff Code | Structure Explanation |
 --- 
| Global Standard | 8534.00 | The 6-digit international heading for all printed circuits. |
| United States | 8534.00.0040 | The HTSUS code specifies "Plastics impregnated, multilayered" with 4 layers or less. |
| European Union | 8534.00.19 | The 8-digit CN code for multilayered printed circuits. |
| Singapore | 8534.00.90 | This local code covers many multilayered circuits, reflecting its trade focus. | [...] United States (HTSUS): The US uses the Harmonized Tariff Schedule of the United States, which extends the code to 10 digits. These last four digits provide incredible specificity, differentiating products to apply various trade agreement benefits or, in some cases, punitive tariffs.

results.title: HS Code for PCB Assembly: A Guide for Global Trade Compliance
results.content:
The correct classification for PCB assemblies is:

### HS Code 8537.10 or 8537.20

Depending on whether the assembly:

 contains switching/controlling functions,
 forms a control panel, or
 is part of a machine or system.

Another relevant category:

### HS Code 8543.70 — Other Electronic Assemblies

Used for specialized or non-defined electronic modules.

Important:  
There is no single universal HS Code for PCB assembly because classification depends on: [...] | PCBA Type | Typical Classification | Notes |
 --- 
| Bare PCB | 8534.00 | No components mounted |
| Fully assembled PCB | 8537.x or 8543.70 | Depends on intended use |
| Power supply boards | 8504.x | If they operate as standalone power units |
| RF modules | 8517.x | Telecommunications-related |
| Control boards | 8537.10 | Industrial controls likely fall here |
| Medical module assemblies | Varies | Requires device-based classification | [...] For electronics, these codes exist under Chapter 85, which covers electrical machinery.

## The Core HS Code for PCB Assembly

PCB assemblies (PCBA) fall under:

### HS Code 8534.00 — Printed Circuits

But here’s the nuance:  
This specific subheading only covers bare PCBs, not assembled boards.

When electronic components are mounted using SMT or through-hole processes, the product becomes an assembled electronic board, shifting classification.

These rules make sure the code fits the product and follows the law. HS codes help everyone use the same system around the world.

### Main HS Code for PCB SMT and Assembly [...] The main HS code for printing circuit board products is 8534.00.00. This HS code for printing circuit board specifically applies to bare PCB items. Using the correct HS code for printing circuit board is essential for smooth customs clearance. It helps companies avoid delays and extra costs during shipping. Customs officials and shipping partners rely on this HS code for printing circuit board to classify shipments and determine duty rates.
